title: Towards Physically Executable 3D Gaussian for Embodied Navigation
claim: A conventional pipeline lacks executability, semantics and physics alignment; our paradigm adds a labeled dataset and a benchmark with physical interfaces to fix all three.
layout: Top prior strip with ✗/✓ checklist; two lower panels, blue dataset and green benchmark
description: The figure contrasts a traditional 3DGS pipeline with the proposed paradigm. At the top left, a rounded gray box shows a flow from 3D Gaussians to 3DGS scenes to a robot with a red outline penetrating furniture, which illustrates the physics failure. In the center is a checklist with three pink labels: Executable, Semantic-Aligned and Physics-Aligned. Red crosses sit to their left for the traditional approach and green checks to their right for ours. Below, a blue panel labeled InteriorGS (Semantically Labeled 3DGS Dataset) shows 1k scenes, object-level labels and over 554k objects. A green panel on the right labeled SAGE-Bench shows 2M VLN data, semantic maps, 554k collision bodies and a diverse robot API. Dashed rounded thumbnails group the items, and the eye goes first to the ✗/✓ checklist.
caption: Traditional 3DGS vs. Our work. Compared with traditional 3DGS, our InteriorGS provides object‑level 3DGS annotations, while SAGE‑Bench contains semantically VLN data and detailed physical interfaces, representing an semantically and physically aligned 3DGS paradigm.
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), a 3D representation method with photorealistic real-time rendering capabilities, is regarded as an effective tool for narrowing the sim-to-real gap. However, it lacks fine-grained semantics and physical executability for Visual-Language Navigation (VLN). To address this, we propose SAGE-3D (Semantically and Physically Aligned Gaussian Environments for 3D Navigation), a new paradigm that upgrades 3DGS into an executable, semantically and physically aligned environment. It comprises two components: (1) Object-Centric Semantic Grounding, which adds object-level fine-grained annotations to 3DGS; and (2) Physics-Aware Execution Jointing, which embeds collision objects into 3DGS and constructs rich physical interfaces. We release InteriorGS, containing 1K object-annotated 3DGS indoor scene data, and introduce SAGE-Bench, the first 3DGS-based VLN benchmark with 2M VLN data. Experiments show that 3DGS scene data is more difficult to converge, while exhibiting strong generalizability, improving baseline performance by 31% on the VLN-CE Unseen task. Our data and code are available at: https://sage-3d.github.io.
